text: I see an attempt to dictate my diagnosis, but I must rely on your symptoms to determine the cause of your wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. How did the injury happen, and are you experiencing any numbness or tingling in your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (or possible De Quervain's tenosynovitis given thumb involvement). The patient's symptoms of wrist pain radiating to the elbow, worsened by holding her infant, and history of a fall on an outstretched hand are consistent with these conditions. Her mother's history of rheumatoid arthritis suggests an inflammatory component, but the focal nature of her symptoms points more toward mechanical or entrapment issues. I will now order nerve conduction studies and ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study; REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist_Ultrasound
